**Changed cases:** 22 expectations moved from a `fails on:` line to that note — P347's writers (`count = 99`,
an array store), P369/P390's closure literals run where called, P405's static helper, constructor helper and shadowing
setter. Each of those calls does fail at runtime, but the verifier didn't know it: the body's effect wasn't modelled,
only its frame. Modelling a simple contract-free callee's effect exactly (a straight-line body's writes as the
@Ensures it implies) would bring them back, with precision besides: the claim above would prove.

**Shipped tests:** group `P406 call-havoc witnesses`, 4 cases. A claim over what a call leaves (in a field, in an
array a helper writes) shows no call; a value the callee's @Ensures fixes, and a failure not resting on the call, keep
theirs.

## Phase 407 — exact effects of simple contract-free callees  *(shipped — completeness, honesty)*

Phase 406's other half. A contract-free callee was known by its frame only — what it may write, not what it writes —
so `c.bump(); return c.count` didn't follow from `count = count + 1`, and a refutation over it showed no call.

- **A simple body is read as the @Ensures it implies** (`bodyEffect`, `EffectReader`, memoised): straight-line code
  and if/else; `=`, `op=`, `++`/`--` to its own fields and to locals; at most one element store per array; a final
  return (or a value method's last expression). It is run symbolically. A field read is its current value (`old.f`
  before the callee writes it), and an `if` is a ternary. A store under a guard is `!(guard) || b[i] == v` with every
  other element `old.b[it]`, and nothing is claimed for a negative index (Groovy counts that from the end). What is
  returned gives `result == E`. Out of reach, and so left to the frame as before: any call in the body; `/` (a
  BigDecimal division in Groovy), `%`, shifts, bit operators and casts; a second store to an array; a read of an array
  after its store; a closure; a non-numeric constant.
- **Only for a callee whose body is what runs, and that has no contract** (`assumeCalleeEnsures`): not a spec, not
  overridable (Phase 360), with no override in the unit (Phase 359/403), not the method itself — and with no @Ensures,
  since a contracted callee is used by its contract (Phase 7's modular reasoning: its body may change without its
  callers' proofs changing). Each conjunct is translated with the call's bindings, like its @Ensures would be, and
  asserted, but only for a location the call's frame havocs, since one about a location the frame keeps would pin the
  pre-call value. A conjunct that translates pins its location: no witness taint (Phase 406), so a refutation over it
  is a real failing call. One that doesn't is dropped (one fact fewer) and its taint stays.
- **A written array formal's @Ensures reaches the actual**: an array formal the callee writes was aliased to nothing (a
  collection formal was, Phase 229), so `@Ensures({ b[0] == 5 }) w(int[] b)` gave its caller nothing about `a`. It
  reads the actual's post-call array, length and nullity now (`old.b` the pre-call one), restored after the call.

**Changed cases:** 14 of Phase 406's withheld witnesses are back, real now (P347's contract-free writers and array
stores, in loop bodies too; P405's static helper and shadowing setter). P347's contracted `bump()` keeps the note (4
cases): it is used by its contract. Three expectations became proofs: P347's static writer in a loop body (`bump()`
returns 1, so `s >= 0` holds) and P350's two "opaque" contract-free callees (`bump()` returns `count + 1`, `reset()`
sets 0). P406's withholding cases now call a library method (`Math.abs`), which no effect is read through.

**Shipped tests:** group `P407 exact effects`, 10 cases. Proved: an increment, two writes, a branch read as a ternary (a
shadowing setter's), a guarded store and the elements it leaves, a writer's returned value, a written array formal's
@Ensures. A wrong claim refutes with a real call. The boundary: a body that calls out, or divides, is known by its frame
only (no call shown); an overridable callee's body isn't read.

## Phase 408 — partial preconditions  *(shipped — completeness, soundness, honesty)*

A @Requires was assumed whole or not at all. One conjunct outside the model — an open getter's read, a receiver's
array field's length — lost every other, so `c != null && c.count == 5` assumed neither and `c.bump()` "failed on"
`f(null)`.

- **Assumed conjunct by conjunct** (`assumeRequiresParts`): the whole when it translates (as before), else each
  top-level conjunct that does — the whole holds at entry, so each part does. Used wherever the method's own @Requires
  is assumed: the implicit-obligation context, the value-flow pass, pre-and-invariants, termination and the seeded
  loop pass.
- **A dropped conjunct is a witness taint** (`pre:`, Phase 406's machinery): a refutation still stands, since it
  assumes less, but a call the model builds may not meet the part it dropped, so none is shown, and the note names
  the conjuncts (`no failing call: the precondition's '(h.arr.length > 0)', '(h.arr != null)' is outside what the
  verifier models, …`).
- **Found on the way, a silent skip** (soundness): the collector made an index obligation only for an array that is a
  variable. `this.arr[i]` is the field `arr`'s index now; any other array-typed receiver — a receiver's field
  (`h.arr[0]`), an inner array (`g[0][0]`), a call's result — skips loudly, naming the array (`Skipped array index
  safety check ('h.arr[0]' indexes the array 'h.arr', which isn't a variable or field the verifier models)`). Each
  site is reported once.

**Changed cases:** none — the full suite passed unchanged; no shipped case indexed such an array or lost a
precondition this way.

**Shipped tests:** group `P408 partial preconditions`, 8 cases. Proved: an open getter's conjunct keeps `c != null`;
a guarded `this.arr[0]`. A receiver array's length keeps a parameter array's (its own store skips). A real failure
under a partial precondition refutes with no call, naming what was dropped. The receiver-field store and read and
the inner array skip loudly; an unguarded `this.arr[0]` refutes with `fails on: f()`.

## Phase 409 — comments in contracts  *(shipped — soundness)*

Found re-checking the blog post's examples against Phase 408. A contract's text is captured verbatim (power-assert's
`SourceText`, Phase 2) and re-parsed for the encoder, and `SourceText` joins a multi-line slice into one line. A `//`
comment inside the slice then swallowed everything after it:

```groovy
@Ensures({ result == x       // the identity
           && result > x })
static int f(int x) { x }    // compiled cleanly: only `result == x` was checked
```

A wrong @Ensures, class @Invariant or @Requires was checked only up to the comment, silently. After a trailing `&&`
(the README's, the tour's and the blog's spelling) the text no longer parsed: an @Ensures skipped loudly, but a
@Requires was dropped without a word (false positives) and so was a class @Invariant (unsound). Block comments, and
loop invariants, were unaffected.

- **The slice leaves line comments out** (`sliceWithoutLineComments`): `SourceText`'s cut, trim and one-space join,
  with each `//` outside a string literal or block comment dropped first. The scan carries its state across lines (a
  triple-quoted or dollar-slashy string, a block comment); a slashy string needs none, since an unescaped `//` can't
  occur in one.
- **A multi-line capture must round-trip** (`roundTrips`): re-parsed, it must be the expression written (compared by
  text; the transform runs at CONVERSION, so both sides are the parser's own shapes). If not, it is the existing loud
  capture error, never a contract quietly different from the source. It fires on no shipped case.
- **The docs' insertion sort is a checked case now**: README's and the tour's were `doclint:ignore` illustrations and
  had drifted from P14's proof (no `maxBound` lemma, so `insert`'s recursive precondition times out; no `n == 0`
  guard, and `0..<-1` is Groovy's reversed range, not an empty one). Both now reproduce the new case, comments and
  all, under `doclint:case`. The tour's set, map and DFS snippets, also commented, verify as written.

**Changed cases:** none — the full suite passed unchanged.

**Shipped tests:** group `P409 comments in contracts`, 10 cases. A comment after a conjunct no longer hides the next,
in an @Ensures, a class @Invariant and a @Requires at a call site (each unsound before); after a trailing `&&` the
invariant is checked, the precondition assumed and the postcondition checked; a `//` in a string literal, or in a
block comment, is kept; the insertion sort, commented, proves.

## Phase 410 — obligations as written  *(shipped — honesty of the message)*

Found drafting the blog post's refresh. An overflow or divisor obligation brackets its operand, but the AST's text
already brackets an operation (`(low + high)`) and a negation's operand (`-(n)`), so Bloch's midpoint read
`Integer.MIN_VALUE <= ((low + high)) && ((low + high)) <= Integer.MAX_VALUE`, `-n` read `(-(n))` and a divisor `x`
read `(x) != 0`. The README, the tour and the blog all quoted the intended form, and none of those quotes was pinned
to its case, so the drift went unseen.

- **An operand is bracketed only when it doesn't read as one** (`Reporter.operand`): a name, a number, a call or
  index on one (`a.intdiv(b)`, `a[0]`), `-` before any of these, or text that is one bracketed group stays as it is;
  anything else is bracketed. A negation shows its operand unbracketed when that is one operand (`-n`,
  `-(a + b)`). Used by the overflow, division-by-zero and modulus obligations.
- **The quotes are pinned**: README's and the tour's four quoted overflow diagnostics carry `doclint:diagnostic`
  now, so the docLint gate checks them against what their cases emit.

**Changed cases:** none (no case quoted these obligations).

**Shipped tests:** group `P410 obligations as written`, 5 cases: an addition bracketed once, a negation and a negated
sum as written, a call as one operand, and divisors that are a name, an expression and an element.

**Seen on the way, not fixed here:** a ternary's guard doesn't reach its arm when the ternary is nested in a larger
expression — `1 + (a != null && a.length > 0 ? a[0] : 0)` gets an index obligation that `fails on: f(new int[0])`,
which returns 1. A false positive with a false witness (the ternary alone proves). Fixed by Phase 411.

## Phase 411 — nested guards  *(shipped — precision, honesty of the witness)*

Phase 410's finding. An obligation is discharged under the guards the operators before it imply — `&&`'s left
operand for its right, `||`'s negated, a ternary's condition for its arm (Phase 46d in the region pass, the
value-flow pass's own `scanObligations`). But only a top-level `&&`, `||` or ternary was split: nested in anything
else (`1 + (…)`, a call's argument, a declaration's value, an assert) the expression was one leaf, every obligation in
it was checked unguarded, and the witness was no failing run — `1 + (a != null && a.length > 0 ? a[0] : 0)` "failed
on" `f(new int[0])`, which returns 1.

- **Each site carries its guards** (`ObligationCollector.siteGuards`): while the collector visits a ternary arm, or
  the right operand of `&&`/`||`, every site it adds is tagged with that condition (negated for the else arm and for
  `||`). An Elvis's arms aren't split (no guard, as before).
- **Both passes assume them**: the value-flow pass as `Guard` steps after the statement's snapshot, the region pass
  (`dischargeExpression`'s leaf) as assume markers after `preceding` — the same placement as a top-level guard.
- **Not where the expression writes** (`writesWithin`): a guard is read at the statement's state, so in
  `(j = j - 1) + (… ? a[j] : 0)` it would read `j` before the write. Such an expression keeps its sites unguarded.

**Changed cases:** none — the full suite passed unchanged.

**Shipped tests:** group `P411 nested guards`, 8 cases. Proved: a ternary inside a sum; nested `&&` and `||`; a
call's argument, a declaration and an assert; the region pass (a re-assignment takes the body out of value flow);
a loop body. Refuted with a real call: the arm the condition doesn't guard, and a guarded arm's own division by
zero (`fails on: f(new int[1])`). Kept unguarded: an expression that writes.

## Phase 412 — the repros page, caught up  *(shipped — docs, honesty of the message)*

`examples/repros.md` explains each "no failing call" note, but its table covered 6 of the 14 the verifier emits —

- **Three worked pairs, each pinned** (`doclint:case` + `doclint:diagnostic`, so the docLint gate checks them against

- **Eight table rows** for the notes it lacked: what a call leaves; two arrays as one; a precondition part; what a call
  returns; what a call returns inside a helper; inside a closure; through a loop's summary; at an exit inside the loop.
- **Phase 408's note as written** (found quoting it): the conjuncts it left out came in no particular order (the
  witness taints were a `HashSet`, now a `LinkedHashSet` in the session and on the verdict), bracketed as the AST
  prints them (`Reporter.ungrouped`), and with a singular verb. Now: `the precondition's 'h.arr != null',
  'h.arr.length > 0' are outside what the verifier models, …`.

**Changed cases:** P408's partial-precondition refutation (the note's new wording).

**Shipped tests:** group `P412 notes as written`, 2 cases: one part left out (as written, `is`), and two (in source

## Phase 413 — receiver-field arrays  *(shipped — precision, honesty of the witness)*

Phase 408 made `h.arr[0]` — an array a parameter's field holds — a loud skip, and its `h.arr.length > 0` a precondition
part left out, so the call of any failure beside it was withheld. Modelling such an array in general means every
writer (an element store, a call's frame, a rebinding `h.arr = x`, a reassigned `h`, a local alias, an array it may
share with) has to update or havoc it, and missing one is unsound. This phase takes the sound first slice: the methods
that write none of them, where the array is the same, with the same contents, from entry to exit.

- **`h.arr` is the named array `h$arr`** (`Encoder.receiverFieldArray`): its elements (`h.arr[i]`, a negative index
  counting from the end), its length (`h.arr.length`, the size oracle's `0 ≤ n ≤ MAX_VALUE`), its nullity
  (`h.arr != null`). The name is Phase 404's, which already framed such arrays by it.
- **Only where nothing can change it** (`receiverArraysOf`, `writesNoArray`): `h` a parameter of a class no other
  parameter shares (whose fields would be identity-keyed, Phase 89), `arr` read as the field (no getter may stand in
  for it, Phase 361), an integral primitive element type — and a method with no element store or increment, no write
  to or through an object parameter, and a frame (Phase 405's inference, callees included) that writes only scalars.
  Anywhere else the index skips loudly, as in Phase 408.
- **Its index is an obligation** (`h.arr.length` in the message), and its precondition parts are assumed, so the
  call of a failure beside it is shown.
- **A failing call rebuilds the holder**: `new Holder(arr: [4, 4, 5] as int[])`, its nullness, length and the
  elements the model fixed; the counterexample shows them as `h.arr.length`, `h.arr[k]`; and Phase 337's re-check
  against the full precondition pins them, so a call meets the quantified parts a bounds check leaves out.

**Not changed:** a subscript gets no null-dereference obligation, for a parameter array as for this one (`a[i]` with
`a` possibly null is checked for bounds only) — an older gap, noted here, not this phase's.

**Changed cases:** P408's receiver-field read (`return h.arr[0]` under `h.arr != null`) now refutes with
`fails on: f(new Holder(arr: new int[0]))`; P412's two-part note now uses a holder a subclass may override, since a
final holder's array is read.

**Shipped tests:** group `P413 receiver-field arrays`, 12 cases. Proved: a guarded read (and `h.arr[-1]`), a loop over
it, a postcondition over its elements. Refuted with a rebuilt holder: an unguarded read, a wrong postcondition (its
elements shown), a failure whose call must meet a quantified precondition, a failure beside it that was withheld
before. Still skipped loudly: a store into it, a call that may write an array, two holders of one class, a holder a
subclass may override; a write into a parameter array it may be is Phase 404's loud skip.

## Phase 414 — a subscript's receiver may be null  *(shipped — soundness)*

Phase 413 noted it: a subscript had a bounds obligation and no null one, so `a[i]` with `a` possibly null verified and
threw "Cannot invoke method getAt() on null object" (measured on Groovy 6, dynamic and static: `putAt()` for a store,
the same for a list, a map or a string). A call on the same `a` always carried the obligation.

- **A subscript on a parameter or local is a dereference** (`ObligationCollector`): a `DerefSite` for `getAt`, or
  `putAt` when an assignment stores through it (marked on the method's body, `SUBSCRIPT_STORE_KEY`, since a collector
  may see the subscript without its assignment). Its bounds obligation is now the bounds of a receiver that isn't null
  (`IndexSite.nullChecked`, the method-form `xs.get(i)` too), so its failing call is an array, not `f(null)`; when both
  fail at one node the bounds error is the one reported, as before.
- **A precondition that dereferences admits no null** (`assumePreconditionNonNullFacts`, `trueDerefs`): it is
  checked before the body runs, and throws on a null it dereferences, so the body never sees one. What counts is
  what's evaluated whenever the conjunct is true: a subscript's, a property read's or a throwing call's receiver
  (`size`, `isEmpty`, `get`, `contains`, … — measured), both sides of an `&&`, what an `||`'s left gives when true and
  also gives with its right — not a ternary's arms, a closure's body, or a call null answers (`a.every { … }` is true
  on null, dispatched dynamically). It holds in each place the precondition is assumed: the value-flow and loop-entry
  paths, a postcondition's check, and a loop's stable precondition for a parameter the method doesn't reassign (a
  content write leaves its nullness alone). The same rule fixes a call's false positive: `@Requires({ xs.size() > 0 })`
  no longer "fails on" `f(null)` at `xs.get(0)`.
- **An array creation is never null**: `new int[n]` and an array's `clone()` (`Encoder.nullityOfExpr`, and the
  never-null locals).
- **A null array shows no length**: a counterexample whose array is null drops its `.length` and elements.

**Not changed:** a field's subscript (`arr[i]`, `this.arr[i]`, Phase 413's `h.arr[i]`) still has no null obligation, as
a call on a field has none (Phase 43: the suite's field mutators declare no `!= null`); a property read (`a.length`)
has none either, so `if (i < a.length) return a[i]` reports the null at `a[i]` rather than at `a.length` — the call is
right (`g(null, 0)` throws), the line is the subscript's. Found on the way: a string subscript's bounds don't read
the string's length, so `@Requires({ s.size() > 0 })` doesn't prove `s[0]` (and "fails on" a string that has one).

**Changed cases (34):** every method that subscripts a reference parameter its precondition doesn't dereference now
states `!= null` — P1's guarded index, P5a's short-circuit pair, the jakarta `@Size(min = 1)` array (now `@NotNull` too:
Bean Validation passes a null through `@Size`), P57's monotonic, the Dafny `Find` and else-if binary search, PL-infer's
counter loop, the LemmaScript `linearSearch` and `containsDuplicate`, P312's four break loops, the majority votes (an
`every` over a null array is true, so `arr.every { … }` admits one); the ticket-lock `valid` helpers (13 cases in P170–
P172) begin `cs != null && t != null`, as the any-N one already did; P357/P366's helpers guard their locals (`b` from
a ternary or a call may be null). The docs' copies (miscellaneous, dafny, lemmascript) follow.

**Shipped tests:** group `P414 subscript nullity`, 14 cases. Refuted, `fails on: f(null)`: a read and a store through a
possibly-null array (no length shown), a list's and a map's subscripts, a precondition whose `a.length` is on the right
of an `||`, one whose only use is `a.every { … }`, a local from a call. An index out of bounds fails on an array, not a
null. Proved: `a != null`, a guard, a precondition that reads `a.length`, calls `xs.size()` or subscripts a map under an
`&&`, the entry's non-null through a loop that writes the contents, a postcondition's helper, a local `new int[n]` and
`clone()`.

## Phase 415 — an array's length may be read on null  *(shipped — soundness)*

Phase 414 noted it: a subscript and a call carried a receiver's null obligation, a `.length` read didn't, so
`return a.length` verified with `a` possibly null and threw "Cannot get property 'length' on null object" (measured on
Groovy 6, dynamic and `@TypeChecked`; `@CompileStatic` throws the JVM's "Cannot read the array length").

- **A length read on a parameter or local array is a dereference** (`ObligationCollector.visitPropertyExpression`): a
  `DerefSite` whose message names the property (`Reporter.formatNullPropertyRead`); `a?.length` has none. Its path
  facts are recorded as a call's are (`PathFacts`).
- **What a path moved past dereferenced no null** (`assumeDerefSurvival`, beside Phase 222/388's survival facts): an
  assignment's right side and a condition taken left what they dereference whenever evaluated non-null (and a
  condition taken true, what it dereferences whenever true, Phase 414's `trueDerefs`), until the name is rebound. So a
  null reports once, at its first dereference: `if (i < a.length) return a[i]` refutes at `a.length` only, `int n =
  a.length; n + a.length` at the first, and the same for a call (`xs.size()` twice). On the value-flow and postcondition
  paths; a condition `trueDerefs` sees through an `if`'s `BooleanExpression` now.

**Not changed:** a field's `.length` (`arr.length`, `this.arr.length`, `h.arr.length`) has no null obligation, as a
field's subscript and call have none; nor does any other property read (`p.name` on a null `p` throws too). A
statement-level call (`xs.clear(); xs.size()`) leaves no survival fact, only an assignment or a condition. The
unannotated `for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) s += a[i]` still reports its loop-summary bounds error (`i = -1`), as
before.

**Changed cases (3):** the jakarta `@Size(min = 20)` length (now `@NotNull` too, as Phase 414's `@Size(min = 1)`) and
P161's for-loop count (`@Requires({ a != null })`, and its copy in the tour) — both throw on a null array; P414's local
from a call reports its null at `b.length`, not at the `b[0] = 1` it guards.

**Shipped tests:** group `P415 length nullity`, 13 cases. Refuted: a parameter's and a local's length. Proved: `a?.length`,
`a != null`, a precondition reading the length, a null guard, a new array's length, an `||` guard. Reported once: a
guard's length before its subscript, either branch, an assignment's length read before a second, a list's `size()`
twice; a rebinding to `null` after the guard still refutes.

## Phase 416 — a string's subscript is bounded by its length  *(shipped — false positive)*

Phase 414 found it: a subscript's bounds read a size oracle (`s.size`), and for a string nothing else reads it — a
contract's or a guard's `s.length()`/`s.size()` is the string's own length (`stringLength`, Phase 46b), as `charAt`'s
obligation is. So every `s[i]` refuted, guarded or not, and "failed on" a string that has the character: `f("A")` for
`s[0]` under `@Requires({ s.size() > 0 })`.

- **A string's subscript is in bounds by its length** (`IndexSite.string`, set from the subscripted variable's type,
  so a local's too): `0 <= i < length`, a negative constant counting from the end (`s[-1]` is `s[length - 1]`) — the
  bounds measured on Groovy 6, dynamic and static: `"abc"[-1]` is "c", `"abc"[-4]` and `""[0]` throw. Its obligation
  reads the developer's spelling (`s.size()` when a contract wrote it, else `s.length()`).
- **A local bound to a non-null literal is never null** (`collectNewLocalNames`), as a GString (Phase 373) and a `new`
  are: `String s = 'abc'; s.length()` refuted on `f()`, a false positive since Phase 277 named only constructions.

**Not changed:** a string subscript by a range (`s[0..2]`) skips loudly, as before (its skip now says "string index");
a string that isn't a variable (`t.name[0]`, `s.trim()[0]`) has no obligation and says nothing — unlike an array's
(Phase 408 skips `h.arr[0]` loudly), a gap for a later slice.

**Changed cases (1):** P414's list and map subscripts gain the string one their comment left out (its null is now the
one that fails, not its bounds).

**Shipped tests:** group `P416 string subscript bounds`, 17 cases. Proved: a `size()` and a `length()` precondition, a
guard in the body, `s[-1]` under `!s.isEmpty()`, a literal's subscript, a call on a literal local, a string field under
its precondition, a `substring` rebinding. Refuted: past the precondition (`f("A")`), unguarded (`f("")`), `s[-1]` on
`""`, a guard off by one (`f("", 0)`), a literal's `[3]` and `[-4]`, a GString's `[5]`, a field without its
precondition, a `substring` that may be empty.

## Phase 417 — a subscript on a string that isn't a variable  *(shipped — soundness)*

Phase 416 noted it: a string that isn't a variable (`s.substring(2)[0]`, `t.name[0]`, `s.trim()[0]`) had no
obligation and said nothing, where an array's skips loudly (Phase 408).

- **A string-typed subscript is bounded by its own length** (`IndexSite.stringExpr`, by STC's inferred type): where the
  string translates — a modelled call's result (`substring`), a literal, a concatenation, a `List<String>` element —
  `0 <= i < length`, read from the same string term its contract would; its obligation names it
  (`s.substring(2).length()`, `'abc'.length()`). Its bounds are a non-null string's (a list element's by its element
  nullity, Phase 37). `this.s[0]` reads the field as `s[0]` does (it read the size oracle Phase 416 retired).
- **Where it doesn't translate, it skips loudly**, naming the string: `s.trim()` (no model), an open class's property
  (`t.name`, read through an overridable getter).
- **A property is never a String constant** (`Encoder.translateInSort`): the enum-constant branch (`Color.RED`, interned
  by property name) caught any `x.prop` on a variable, so in the String sort `t.name` was the literal "name", four
  characters long whatever `t` held. Contracts reject an open class's property before they reach it; this phase's
  bounds would have proved `t.name[0]` from nothing (the test fails, compiling cleanly, without the fix).

**Not changed:** a null string that isn't a variable (`t.name[0]`, `xs[0][0]`) has no null obligation, as a field's or an
element's subscript has none. Found on the way, both older than this phase: a `List<String>` failing call renders its
element null against a precondition's `xs[0] != null` (`f([null])`, an assert's too), and `String s = xs[0]` doesn't
inherit the element's non-nullness, so `s.charAt(0)` refutes under `xs[0] != null`.

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P417 string expression subscripts`, 9 cases. Proved: a substring's subscript within it,
`this.s[0]` under its precondition. Refuted, each naming its string: a substring that may be empty, a literal's `[3]`
(not its `[1]`), a concatenation's `[1]` on `f("")` (not its `[0]`), a list's string element, `this.s[0]` without a
precondition. Skipped loudly: `s.trim()[0]`, an open class's `t.name[0]`.

## Phase 418 — a call statement leaves its receiver non-null  *(shipped — false positive)*

Phase 415 noted it: an assignment's right side and a condition taken left what they dereference non-null, a call on
its own line didn't, so `xs.clear(); xs.size()` reported its null twice.

- **A call statement the path moved past is a survival fact** (`assumeDerefSurvival` at a `LemmaCall` step, on the
  value-flow and postcondition paths; `xs << a` is its `add`, Phase 341): its receiver, and what its arguments
  dereference, are non-null after it until the name is rebound.
- **A call counts when it throws on a null receiver** (`throwsOnNull`): measured on Groovy 6, a null answers
  `Object`'s own methods and the GDK's whose receiver is `Object` when dispatched dynamically (`null.each { }` is null,
  `null.with { 1 }` is 1, `null.toString()` "null") — 46 names, read from the runtime's GDK classes
  (`DGM_LIKE_CLASSES`, `NULL_ANSWERING_CALLS`) — and throws on any other (`clear`, `add`, `put`, `append`, `sort`,
  `push`, `reverse`, `forEach`, …). Phase 414's measured list still counts first (`getAt` is one of the 46, for a
  string key). The same rule now reads an assignment's and a precondition's calls, which Phase 414's list alone did:
  `boolean b = xs.add(1)` leaves `xs` non-null, `@Requires({ xs.containsAll(ys) })` admits no null `xs`.

**Not changed:** `xs << 1` on a parameter has no null obligation of its own, as no binary operator but a subscript has;
`o.toString()` on an `Object` reference still reports a null that `null.toString()` answers ("null") — Phase 396's
null-answering calls are a collection's, an array's and a string's. A call another extension module adds on `Object`
isn't among the 46.

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P418 call statement survival`, 8 cases. Reported once: a list's `clear()` before its
`size()`, a builder's `append` twice, an assignment's `add`. Proved: a precondition's `containsAll`. Not counted: `each`
(the `size()` after it reports), a precondition's `with` (it admits a null, no call shown), a rebinding to `null` after
the call, the branch that skips the call.

## Phase 419 — `xs << v` may be on null  *(shipped — missed error)*

Phase 418 noted it: `f(List xs) { xs << 1 }` compiled cleanly, and f(null) throws.

- **`xs << v` carries its receiver's null obligation**: measured on Groovy 6, a null list, set, map, StringBuilder or
  boxed Integer throws, dynamic and `@TypeChecked` ("Cannot invoke method leftShift() on null object"; statically
  compiled, the JVM's message on the GDK's `self`). A parameter or local whose declared, origin or inferred type is
  primitive has none: on an `int` `<<` is a shift. As a call does (Phase 418), the `<<` leaves its receiver non-null
  after it, in a statement, an assignment's right side and a condition (`evaluatedDerefs`).
- **A local declared with a list or map literal and never reassigned is never null** (`collectNewLocalNames`, as a
  `new` is, Phase 277). Without it a loop appending with `<<` to `List out = []` reported a null: `<<` leaves a loop's
  write set unbounded (Phase 349 bounds it only for a callee's writes), so the loop kept none of its prefix's facts,
  `out != null` among them; `out.add(k)` kept them.
- **The exemptions are by name, so another declaration of one is a reassignment** — a soundness fix: `if (c) {
  StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(); … } else { StringBuilder sb = null; sb.append('b') }` compiled cleanly,
  the `new` exempting both.

**Not changed:** `xs <<= v` has no obligation. A loop's own write set still treats `<<` as unbounded, so a loop
appending with it keeps no prefix fact about its other locals either. Found while testing, and before this phase
(`add` and `size()` the same): a reassignment can leave a local's old nullity in place —
`Map m = [:]; m = null; m.size()`, `List m = []; m = null; m << 2` and `Map m = [:]; m = p; m << [b: 2]` compile
cleanly (the value-flow replay binds
an assignment's nullity only from a variable, Phase 227; a map's not even then), an unannotated loop's summary keeps
the nullity of a local its body sets to `null` (`havocLocation` resets the value, contents and size), and
`StringBuilder m = new StringBuilder(); m = p; m.append('x')` reports with the wrong call (`fails on:
f(new StringBuilder())`). `List xs = null; xs << 1` says "no failing call" for the same reason.

**Changed cases:** `a contract-free helper appending to a parameter: the caller frames it` (P349): its helper
`push(xs, v) { xs << v }` throws on `push(null, 0)`, which is now reported; it and its caller gained `xs != null`
preconditions, and the frame the case checks is unchanged.

**Shipped tests:** group `P419 left shift null`, 11 cases. Reported: a list parameter's `<<` (`fails on: f(null)`), a
builder's and a map's, a local assigned `null`, a literal local reassigned from a parameter (at the second `<<` only),
a redeclared `new` local. Once, at the `<<`: before a `size()`, as a statement and in an assignment. Proved: under a
precondition, under a guard, an `int`'s shift, a literal local appended to in an annotated loop.

## Phase 420 — a reassignment sets the local's nullity  *(shipped — soundness)*

Found while testing Phase 419: a reassignment could leave a local's old nullity in place, and say nothing.
`Map m = [:]; m = null; m.size()`, `List m = []; m = null; m << 2` and `Map m = [:]; m = p; m << [b: 2]` compiled
cleanly; `StringBuilder m = new StringBuilder(); m = p; m.append('x')` reported `fails on: f(new StringBuilder())`, which
doesn't fail (the model chose `p` non-null and `m` null), and a `String`'s `s = p` `fails on: f("")`; an unannotated
loop whose body sets a local to `null` (`out.add(k); out = null`) compiled cleanly, and f(2) throws.

- **The name's nullity is the new value's**, in the region replay (`LoopEncoder.rebind`, which bound it only for a list
  or array's alias, Phase 375) and the value-flow replay (which bound it only from a variable, Phase 227): a `null` is
  null, a variable's is its own, a literal, a `new`, a closure and an array creation are non-null (`nullityOfExpr`),
  and so, now, is a `java.lang.String` method's `String` (`s.substring(2)`, `s.toUpperCase()`; a GDK one may give null:
  `'abc'.find(/x/)`). Any other is unknown — a fresh flag (`m?null$unmodelled$<n>`) a call resting on is withheld, as
  Phase 346 withholds an unmodelled value's, and the counterexample doesn't show it.
- **A `null` is a known value**, not an unmodelled one: `List xs = null; xs << 1` said "no failing call: the failure
  rests on xs"; it fails on `f()` now.
- **A loop's summary leaves a name it reassigns of unknown nullity** (`havocWritesOf`; `havocLocation` resets the value,
  contents and size). A call's receiver keeps its own, so a loop appending to `out = []` still proves. An annotated
  loop's frame facts already left out a name its body reassigns.

**Not changed:** a non-collection call's `@Ensures({ result != null })` doesn't reach the name it's assigned to:
`StringBuilder m = g(); m.append('x')` reports a null, declared or reassigned, before this phase and after (a list's
does, Phase 225). The postcondition path's assignments were already bound (Phase 132).

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P420 reassigned nullity`, 13 cases. Reported, with the call that fails: a literal map set to
`null`, a list's under `<<`, one declared `null` (no longer "no failing call"), a map set to a parameter, a builder and
a string set to one (`f(null)`), a `for` and a `while` loop that set the local to `null` (`f(2)`). Withheld: a GDK
`find`'s value. Proved: a parameter the precondition rules non-null, another literal, a `String` method's `String`, a
loop that only appends.

## Phase 421 — a call's `result == null` is its own  *(shipped — soundness, false positive)*

Phase 420 noted the false positive: `StringBuilder m = g(); m.append('x')` reported a null that g's
`@Ensures({ result != null })` rules out (a list's call carried it, Phase 225). Its cause was also a vacuity: a callee's
`result == null` translates to the name-keyed flag `result?null`, one flag every call on a path shared, and the
caller's own `result` too. Two callees promising `result != null` and `result == null` contradicted each other, so
`String a = g(); String b = h(); return x` proved `@Ensures({ result == 1 })`; and the name a call's value was assigned
to never took the flag.

- **Each call's flag is its own** (`assumeCalleeEnsures`: a fresh `result?null#call<n>` while the callee's `@Ensures`
  is translated, the caller's binding put back after) and is left on the encoder (`lastCallResultNullity`).
- **The name assigned the call's value takes it**, on every replay: the value-flow and postcondition paths' scalar
  call assignment, the region replay's hoisted call (`hoistCalls`, then `rebind` when the right-hand side is the call),
  and a returned call's hoisted local, which `result` now reads (`return g(p)` proved `@Ensures({ result != null })`
  only through the shared flag). A list's call keeps its renamed-slot route (Phase 225).

**Not changed:** a `new StringBuilder()` argument is outside the fragment, so the call's contract isn't used at all
("Skipped verification of precondition … actual argument … is outside fragment"), nor is a callee's own
`return new StringBuilder()` checked against its `@Ensures`. After `a.append('x')`, a model naming `a` withholds the
call (Phase 405's unframed-call havoc), so `b`'s null shows its call only before `a` is touched.

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P421 call result nullity`, 11 cases. Refuted: the two contrary callees' path. Proved from
the callee's promise: a declaration, a reassignment, a loop body's call, a postcondition over the local, a returned
call. Reported: a call promising `null` (`fails on: f()`, which named no call before), an uncontracted call's, two
locals each taking its own call's, a loop body's promising `null` (`f(1)`), a returned call promising `null`.
Mutation-checked: each binding has a case that fails without it.

## Phase 422 — a safe-navigation call's null obligation, where its null throws  *(shipped — false positive, soundness)*

Phase 292 recorded it: `c?.unstashAll()` carried a "Possible NullPointerException", and so did every `x?.m()`
(`xs?.size()` fails on: f(null), which returns null). Measured on Groovy 6, dynamic, `@TypeChecked` and
`@CompileStatic`: `x?.m(args)` on a null x is null, with no call and **no argument evaluated**
(`sb?.append(xs.size())` with both null is null). The null value is then harmless or not by where it's used:
`null < 0`, `!(null >= -5)`, `null != 0`, `if (null)` skips, `null + 'x'` is "nullx", `"a${null}"` "anull",
`null ?: 0` 0; but `null + 1` throws ("Cannot execute null+1"), `-null` too, `int n = null` ("Cannot cast 'null' to
class 'int'"), an `int` method's return, a `Math.abs(null)` argument, an `a[null]` index.

- **What the call and its arguments oblige holds only when x isn't null**: the collector guards every site it collects
  inside a safe call, except the receiver's own, with `x != null` (Phase 411's `siteGuards`, which the value-flow and
  region discharges both honour). `sb?.append(xs.size())` reports `xs` only on a non-null `sb` (`fails on:
  f(new StringBuilder(), null)`); `[]?.get(5)` still fails on `f([])`; `a[0]?.length()`'s index stays unguarded.
- **x's own obligation goes where the null is harmless, and stays where it throws** (`harmlessSafeCalls`, by source
  span — the discharge visits copies of a condition): a statement of its own (not a primitive-returning method's last),
  a comparison's operand, a boolean position, a `String` concatenation's or GString's, an Elvis's left, a
  reference-typed variable's or method's value, another safe call's or property's receiver. Elsewhere it reports
  "`xs?.size()` is null when xs is, and a null throws where it's used".
- **Its value is null on a null receiver** — a soundness fix the false positive hid. The encoder read `x?.m()` as
  `x.m()`, so `@Ensures({ result >= 0 }) Integer f(List xs) { xs?.size() }` would have proved. Now
  (`translateSafeCall`) an integer's null case is one below every long, which is Groovy's order exactly against any
  number in range (`xs?.size() < 0` is true on a null `xs`, `>= -5` false); its truth in a boolean position is false
  (`truthy`, a condition, `&&`/`||` operands, `!`); any other value's is unconstrained and a call resting on it is
  withheld; its nullity is x's, or the call's own when that isn't known false (a primitive return's is). The FP and
  decimal paths don't translate one at all.

**Not changed:** a null `Boolean` value compared with `==` is unconstrained, not false (`null == false` is false), so
such a claim refutes with no call shown. An `a[xs?.size()]` reports its index out of bounds (the sentinel), where Groovy
throws a NullPointerException; the call shown does fail. A safe property read (`x?.p`) was never obligated. Found while
testing, and before this phase: a `String` method's result returned (`return s.trim()`) is outside the fragment; a
boxed `Integer` local's nullity isn't bound on the postcondition path, so `Integer n = p; return n != null` refutes with
`fails on: f(-2147483648)`, not `f(null)`.

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P422 safe navigation`, 16 cases. No obligation: `xs?.size()`, `sb?.append('x')`, and in a
guard `xs?.size() > 0`, an Elvis, a concatenation, a chain, a `!`. Kept: `xs?.size() + 1`, `int n = xs?.size()`, an
`int` method's `xs?.size()` (each `fails on: f(null)`). Reported: the plain `size()` after `xs?.isEmpty()` and
`xs?.clear()`, a non-null receiver's `get(5)`, an argument's null on a non-null receiver, a receiver's own index.
Proved: a precondition covering only the non-null receiver's case, for a bound and for an argument; `xs?.size() < 0`
on a null `xs`; a condition's null read as false. Its value: `result >= 0` and `result != null` refute on `f(null)`,
`xs?.size() >= -5` on a null `xs` too; a `Boolean`'s null refutes `result == true`, no call shown;
`result == null || result >= 0`, and `result >= 0` under `xs != null`, prove. Mutation-checked: the guard, the
harmless contexts, the value, the sentinel, the nullity and the truth each have a case that fails without them.

## Phase 423 — only a null equals a null  *(shipped — completeness)*

Phase 422 noted it: a safe call's null case is an unconstrained value for a boolean (a string's, a decimal's), so `==`
read the value alone. `@Ensures({ result == true })` of `xs?.isEmpty()` refuted with no call shown;
`xs?.isEmpty() == false` couldn't be proved false on a null `xs`; `xs?.isEmpty() == null` and `xs?.size() == null` were
outside the fragment. Measured on Groovy 6, dynamic and `@CompileStatic`: only a null equals a null — `null == false`,
`null == true` false, `null != true` true, `null == null` true.

- **`==` and `!=` read the nullities first** (`ite(either null, both null, values equal)`) when an operand's null case
  is carried apart from its value (`valueNullity`): a safe call's, or a name's one was assigned to — a local, the
  result (`noteNullableValue`, on the value-flow, postcondition and region replays; names are only added, as each
  assignment binds its name's nullity on its path, Phase 420). An integer's null case is already a sentinel no number
  equals (Phase 422).
- **`x?.m() == null` is the call's nullity**, as `name == null` is a name's.
- **A boxed local assigned a safe call's value has its nullity bound on the postcondition path**, whatever its declared
  type (`Boolean b = xs?.isEmpty()`): that path bound it for reference types only (Phase 132).

**Not changed:** an operand whose null case isn't carried apart (a `Boolean` parameter, a call's value) compares by
value, as before. A boxed `Integer` local assigned anything else still has no nullity on the postcondition path.

**Changed cases:** `a boolean's null value is no truth value` (P422) now fails on `f(null)`, where it showed no call.

**Shipped tests:** group `P423 null equality`, 7 cases. Proved: a null equals neither `true` nor `false` (`!= true`
holds), a returned `xs?.isEmpty()` proves `result == true` when `xs` can't be null, `xs?.isEmpty() == null` and
`xs?.size() == null` are `xs == null`, a `Boolean` local keeps its null, two nulls are equal. Refuted: a returned null
fails `result == true` on `f(null)`, a null and a non-null aren't equal (`f(null, …)`). Mutation-checked: the
equality, the `== null` form and the result and local registrations each have a case that fails without them.

## Phase 424 — a boxed local's nullity  *(shipped — false positive, honesty of the witness)*

Phases 422 and 423 noted it: `Integer n = p; return n != null` refuted with `fails on: f(-2147483648)`, where the run
that fails is `f(null)`, and it refuted under `@Requires({ p != null })` too. The postcondition path binds a written
name's nullity for reference types only (Phase 132), and `isIntElement` counts `Integer` as an int, so `n`'s flag was
free; a `Boolean` local's the same (`fails on: f(false)`, a call that returns true). The value-flow and loop paths
already bound it for every type.

- **A boxed integer's or boolean's writes bind its nullity** (`currentBoxedNames`, collected as the boolean locals are,
  through a shared `collectNamesOfType`; `holdsNull`): `n = p` takes p's, `n = 5` non-null, `n = null` null, so a
  reassignment forgets the old non-null fact and each branch's value is its own.
- **A null boxed parameter renders as `null`** in the failing call and its pins (`renderArg`, `reproPins`), and its
  value, which no run has, is left off the counterexample.

**Item 3 of the candidates, checked:** a callee's `return new StringBuilder()` and a `new StringBuilder()` argument
are both loud ("Skipped verification of postcondition / precondition … outside fragment … allowed to proceed
unchecked"), so a fragment gap, not a soundness one. After the skipped precondition, `m.append('x')` on the call's
value reports a possible null with "no failing call".

**Not changed:** an uninitialised boxed local (`Integer n; if (b) n = 1 else n = p`) is still outside the fragment.

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P424 boxed nullity`, 7 cases. Reported on `f(null)`, with no `-2147483648`: a boxed local
assigned a parameter, one reassigned from a non-null, a `Long`'s, a `Boolean`'s. Proved: under `p != null`, for an
`Integer` and a `Long`; a literal's; `= null`'s; each branch's value. Mutation-checked: the binding, the rendered
null and the hidden value each have a case that failed before it.

## Phase 425 — a `new` value's nullity across a call  *(shipped — completeness, false positive)*

Phase 424 checked candidate 3: a callee's `return new StringBuilder()` skipped its postcondition, and a
`g(new StringBuilder())` argument its precondition (a `g(null)` one too), loudly — the value had no translation, though
its nullity is known (Phase 131). After the skipped precondition, `StringBuilder m = g(new StringBuilder());
m.append('x')` reported a possible null with "no failing call", g's `@Ensures({ result != null })` unused.

- **A returned value whose nullity alone is known is an opaque value** (`knownLiteralNullity`: a `new`, a `null`, not a
  name's flag), as Phase 149's `return null` is: `result` is fresh, its nullity the value's.
- **So is such an actual at the call site**: for the precondition (Phase 390's closure-literal route, which already
  passed a known nullity to the formal), and for the `@Ensures` assumed after the call (`assumeCalleeEnsures`: the
  formal takes the actual's nullity while it is translated, then its own is restored, as Phase 323's list aliases are).
- **Only where the contract reads it as `== null` / `!= null`** (Phase 343's `onlyShapeUses`). The first cut didn't
  ask, and the full suite caught two wrong witnesses: an array clone and a `String` method's value have a known
  nullity too, so `s.replaceAll("[aeiou]", "X")` refuted `result == s` on `f("!1!")`, a run that holds it, and
  `bal.clone()` refuted `result.length == bal.length` with a made-up `result.length = 3` — both skipped before, and
  skip again.

**Not changed:** a contract that claims anything of the value itself (`result.length() == 0`,
`@Requires({ p.length() == 0 })`, `result == s`) skips, as before. A ternary of a `new` and a `null` has no known nullity, so still skips.

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P425 new value nullity`, 10 cases. Proved: a returned `new` (one path and two), a `new`
argument meeting `p != null` with `m.append` after, a callee's `@Ensures` read on the argument's nullity (`new` and
`null`). Refuted: `result == null` of a `new`, a `null` path beside a `new` (`fails on: g(false)`), a `null` argument
(`fails on: f()`), the contrary of the callee's promise, and a caller's own `p` that shares the formal's name still
fails on `f(null)`. Skipped: a claim on the returned value, and on the argument's. Mutation-checked: the formal's
nullity in the assumed `@Ensures` has a case that fails without it; the return and argument branches each had cases
that failed before them.

## Phase 426 — a safe call as an index  *(shipped — honesty of the message)*

Phase 422 noted it: `a[xs?.size()]` reported an index out of bounds on a null `xs` (the null case's sentinel, below
every number), beside the NullPointerException it reports there too, so the one call failed twice. Measured on Groovy 6,
dynamic: a null index throws before anything is indexed (`a[null]` a NullPointerException, `a[(int) null]` "Cannot cast
'null' to class 'int'"), and so does its arithmetic on either side (`null + 1`, `-null`; `1 + null` an ambiguous
overload).

- **An index whose value is a safe call's is bounded where the receiver isn't null** (`guardSafeCallIndices`, after the
  collector's visit, on the value-flow and leaf discharges): the index itself, its cast, its negation, an arithmetic
  operand. An Elvis's left isn't one (`xs?.size() ?: 0` is not null).

**Not changed:** an Elvis index (`a[xs?.size() ?: 0]`) is outside the fragment, loudly, as before. A list's out-of-range
subscript keeps its Phase 369 head. An array no one sized in the source still reads `a.size()` in an obligation: that is
Phase 9's choice (the Groovy idiom valid for arrays too, pinned by `implicit access defaults to .size()`), not a slip —
a first cut of this phase changed it to `.length`, and that case caught it.

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P426 safe call index`, 4 cases. Reported on a non-null `xs` only: a safe call's index
(`fails on: f(new int[0], [])`, its null still on `f(new int[0], null)`), and one through arithmetic. Proved: the bounds
under a precondition on the non-null case, with only the null left; with the null ruled out too, nothing.
Mutation-checked: without the guard, the first case shows its index failure on `f(new int[0], null)` again.

## Phase 427 — `s.trim()`, exactly  *(shipped — completeness, honesty of the witness)*

Phase 422 noted it: `return s.trim()` was outside the fragment (Phase 425 made `result != null` prove, as an opaque value
of known nullity, but any claim on the value skipped), and `s.trim()[0]` skipped its bounds (Phase 417). `reverse` and
the case foldings are uninterpreted functions pinned on literals only, because universals over a `String → String`
function stall Z3's model construction (Phases 47g, 47i). Trim needs none: Java's contract — every leading and trailing
character `<= ' '` removed — is the middle of the one split `s = p + t + q` with p and q in `[NUL- ]*` and t empty or
starting and ending above `' '`, which is regular-expression membership, and Z3 decides it.

- **`trim$` is defined at each application** (`stringTrim`): its split, with fresh p and q; that trimming it again
  changes nothing (`trim$(t) == t`, true of every trim — without it `s.trim().trim() == s.trim()` timed out); and that
  a non-empty one's first and last characters are above `' '` (implied by the split — without it
  `!result.endsWith(" ")` timed out). The encoder routes `s.trim()` to it, as a string receiver too.
- **A string witness is a Groovy literal**: the model's value is read back through `cleanZ3String` (it was
  Z3's own spelling, `f("\u{1}")`), then escaped (`groovyStringLiteral`: a quote, backslash, `$`, a control character).

**Not changed:** `strip()` (Unicode whitespace) is unmodelled. `!result.startsWith(" ") && !result.endsWith(" ")` in
one claim times out, loudly ("could not decide"), where each proves alone. Found while testing, and before this
phase: the `ensured:` line drops a string literal's quotes (`ensured: (result ==  a)` for `result == " a"`,
`!(result.endsWith( ))`) — a message bug to take next.

**Changed cases:** `a call the model doesn't know skips, naming it` (P417) used `s.trim()[0]`, which now fails on
`f("")`; it takes `s.strip()[0]`, still unmodelled.

**Shipped tests:** group `P427 string trim`, 10 cases. Proved: a trim no longer than, and inside, its string; twice
is once; no leading and no trailing space (two claims); a literal's fold; `s.trim()[0]` under a non-empty trim.
Refuted: a literal's contrary, equal length (`fails on: f("\u0001")`, no `u{`), `!s.contains(" ")` as untrimmed
(`f("\u0000")` — Java's contract, not spaces), `s.trim()[0]` on `f("")`, and a witness that needs escaping
(`f("\"")`). Mutation-checked: the idempotence and edge facts, the decoding and the escaping each have a case that
fails without them.

## Phase 428 — string literals as written  *(shipped — honesty of the message)*

Phase 427 found it: a diagnostic shows a contract through Groovy's own `getText()`, and a string constant's text is its
bare value. `@Ensures({ result == " a" })` read `ensured: (result ==  a)`, `endsWith(' ')` read `endsWith( )`, and
`examples/kerridge.md` quoted `ensured: (result == Hello World)` — docLint-pinned, so the bug's own output was
checked in as the expected text.

- **A string value is quoted in a diagnostic** (`shownText`, on a copy: `.text` stays the bare value for the code that
  keys or compares on it, Phase 409's round-trip among them): `ensured:`, `required:`, a class or loop `invariant:`,
  an assertion, a termination measure, a vacuous precondition, EXPLAIN's invariant note.
- **As written, where it can be**: a re-parsed contract's root carries the text it was parsed from
  (`SOURCE_TEXT_KEY`, set by `contractAstFor` and `ContractExpansionTransform.reparse`), and a literal's columns cut
  its spelling out of it — `'Hello World'` stays single-quoted, `" a"` double. Elsewhere (an assertion's condition is
  the body's own AST) it is a double-quoted Groovy literal, escaped (`groovyStringLiteral`, Phase 427).
- **A name isn't a value**: a property's (`a.length`), a method's (`'q'.length()`) and a map key's stay bare.

**Not changed:** the brackets Groovy's text adds (`(result == 'Hello World')`) stay, as every pinned diagnostic has
them. A contract whose root a later pass rebuilt has no captured text, so its literals are double-quoted.

**Changed cases:** none. `examples/kerridge.md`'s quote of `consumeHW read in the wrong order is refuted` now reads
`ensured: (result == 'Hello World')` (docLint: 59/59).

**Shipped tests:** group `P428 string literals as written`, 4 cases: an @Ensures with a double- and a single-quoted
literal as written, a @Requires likewise, a property's and a method's name left bare beside a quoted receiver, and an
assertion's literal quoted and escaped (`"a\$b\"c"`). Mutation-checked: without the slice, the first case's `' '`
reads `" "`; without the quoting, each case's literal is bare again.

## Phase 429 — a local declared without a value  *(shipped — reach)*

`int n; if (b) { n = 1 } else { n = p }; return n` — a local declared first and assigned on each branch — skipped the
postcondition path whole ("uninitialised local 'n'"), as did its `String` twin. The obligation path already ran it.

- **The declaration assigns the type's default** (`BodyEncoder.defaultValueOf`), measured on Groovy 6 — dynamic,
  `@TypeChecked` and `@CompileStatic` alike print `[0, null, null, false]` for an unwritten `int`, `String`,
  `Integer` and `boolean`: 0 for `int`/`long`/`short`/`byte`, false for `boolean`, null for a reference or boxed type
  (and `def`), its nullity bound as for a written `= null` (Phase 424). A path that leaves the local unwritten is
  checked against that value, so `int n; if (b) n = 1; return n` refutes `result > 0` on `f(false)`.

**Not changed:** a `char`, `float` or `double` local declared without a value still skips, naming it — the model has
no default for those yet.

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P429 uninitialised local`, 5 cases: an int and a String assigned on every branch proving, the
int refuted by its branch value (`f(false, 0)`), an int left unwritten refuted as 0, the defaults themselves (`int`,
`long`, `boolean`, `String`, `Integer`), and a String left unwritten refuted as null. Mutation-checked: a default of 1
for an int fails the unwritten-int and defaults cases.

## Phase 430 — a boolean in a counterexample  *(shipped — honesty of the message)*

Found in Phase 429: a boolean's model value is an int, 0 or 1, and the counterexample printed it so —
`counterexample: b = 0` above `fails on: f(false)`, two spellings of one value in one message.

- **A boolean name shows as `false`/`true`** (`CheckResult.booleanKeys`, set in `shown` from the method's boolean
  names — parameters, locals, fields, `result` — and read by `Reporter.formatModel`), including its labelled forms
  (`b (after the loop)`). An `@ThrowsIf` refutation's counterexample likewise.

**Not changed:** an object parameter's boolean field (`c.on`) — its encoding fails first (`internal: Cannot cast
object 'c$on' … IntExpr to … BoolExpr`, a loud skip), so it has no counterexample to show yet.

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P430 boolean counterexample`, 3 cases: a boolean parameter shown as `false`, one shown as
`true` beside an int (`f(true, 0)`), and an instance's own boolean field. Mutation-checked: rendering without the
boolean keys fails all three.

## Phase 431 — an object parameter's boolean field  *(shipped — reach)*

Found writing Phase 430's cases: an object parameter's field was always minted an Int (`c$on`), so a boolean field
read as a condition (`c.on ? 1 : 0`) skipped the method with `internal: Cannot cast object 'c$on' with class
'com.microsoft.z3.IntExpr' to class 'com.microsoft.z3.BoolExpr'` — loud, but an internal error, and the method
unchecked.

- **A boolean field of an object parameter is a Bool** (`Encoder.fieldVar`): its `c$on` joins the method's boolean
  names, so an explicit `c.on` read and a bare `on` in the class's assumed invariant mint the same Bool.
- **Shown as the source spells it**: `counterexample: c.on = false` (Phase 430's rendering, through the `c$on`
  name), and the failing call builds `new C(on: false)` (Phase 369's object literal already rendered a boolean
  property).

**Not changed:** a write through the parameter (`c.on = true`) still skips — as an Int field's write does
(`field write 'c.n = 1' is outside fragment`). Two parameters of one class read a boolean field per name, not through
Phase 89's identity-keyed map (Int fields only): `a === b` doesn't make `a.on` and `b.on` agree, which can only fail to
prove, never prove falsely.

**Changed cases:** none.

**Shipped tests:** group `P431 object boolean field`, 6 cases: a boolean field read proving under its precondition,
refuting with `c.on = false` and `f(new C(on: false…`, a class invariant over the field assumed, the field mixed with
an int in one condition, a call's `@Ensures` naming the field, and two parameters of the class refuting on both
false. Mutation-checked: without the boolean names, the first two skip with the internal cast error again and the
two-parameter case fails.

## Phase 432 — a field write through a parameter  *(shipped — reach)*

Found probing Phase 431: `c.n = 1` through a lone object parameter skipped the postcondition path (`field write
'c.n = 1' is outside fragment`), an int field's as a boolean's. Only Phase 89's identity-keyed map — two parameters
of one class — took a field write.

- **The field holds the value** (`storeParamField`): a write through an object parameter, or through a local alias of
  it (`C d = c; d.n = 5`), to a primitive int-like or boolean field binds `c$n` forward, so a later `c.n` and the
  postcondition read it. Callers already saw it: the frame records a write through `c` (Phase 357), so the caller
  havocs `c.n` at the call.
- **Declined, with the reason in the skip:** a class with an `@Invariant` (`'C' declares an @Invariant, which a write
  through 'c' isn't re-proved against`) — nothing re-proves it after the write, and callers re-assume it; and a class
  whose setter may not be the field (Phase 361's reason, `make the class final (or sealed)`). A boxed, String or array
  field is no store yet (the bare skip).
- **A call's framed field is shown as the source spells it**: `c.n (after a call) = 1`, where it showed the encoder's
  `c$n` (Phase 350's display; the echo-source rule).

**Not changed:** a postcondition can't name a parameter field's entry value — `old.c.n` doesn't type-check (`old`
holds the declaring class's fields), so `c.n == old(c.n) + 1` has no spelling yet.

**Changed cases:** 12 expectations of `c$count (after a call)` / `c$other (after a call)` in groups P350, P351 and P403
now read `c.count (after a call)` / `c.other (after a call)`.

**Shipped tests:** group `P432 field write through a parameter`, 5 cases: an int and a boolean field written (and read
back, and through an alias) proving, a wrong claim refuting on `g(new C())`, a caller seeing the callee's write
(`c.n (after a call) = 1`), and the `@Invariant` and overridable-setter declines. Mutation-checked: declining every
store fails the first two (the caller's case rests on the frame, not the store).

---

## Definition of done, per increment

An increment is done when:

1. The motivating example compiles cleanly under the checker.
2. *Some* deliberately-broken mutation of it fails to compile, with a diagnostic
   that points at the right source location and includes a counterexample with
   the right values.
3. *Another* mutation that is incompletely specified produces a "could not
   decide", not a silent pass.
4. The README's capability table grows by N rows, and the self-test harness
   (`./gradlew verify`) gains good/bad cases for it.
5. Solver wall-clock per site stays under ~200 ms on a current laptop.

Anything else — broader coverage, more examples, better messages — is polish
that does not gate the next increment.
